breaking.headline: Ukraine launches nearly 1,200 drones at Russia in one of the war's biggest attacks
breaking.fact: Ukraine fired almost 1,200 drones at Russian targets overnight Nov. 12-13, one of its biggest aerial attacks since Moscow's full-scale invasion nearly five years ago. Russia says air defenses downed 1,198 drones, including 467 headed for the Moscow region; strikes that got through killed seven people in three Russian regions, including a 12-year-old. Ukraine says it hit an oil refinery in Volgograd, starting a fire, while Russia answered with 117 drones, killing at least two in Ukraine, including a 17-year-old.

breaking.headline: Congo's Ebola outbreak tops 11,000 cases, deadliest in the country's history
breaking.fact: Congo's Ebola outbreak has passed 11,000 cases — 11,042 infected and 5,387 dead, nearly half of those infected — the deadliest outbreak in Congo's history and the second-largest ever recorded. The Bundibugyo virus has no approved vaccine or treatment and has spread to eight of the country's 26 provinces; six months in, Doctors Without Borders says the outbreak remains out of control, and experts doubt it can be contained within a year.

breaking.headline: Hamas confirms its Rafah brigade commander was killed in an Israeli strike
breaking.fact: Hamas confirmed Sunday that its Rafah Brigade commander, Samir Abu Younis, 53, was killed in an Israeli drone strike Saturday in al-Mawasi, Khan Younis. Israel's military and the Shin Bet said they targeted a senior Hamas commander; the strike hit a tent sheltering displaced people, wounding two. Gaza's Health Ministry says 16 people were killed and 68 wounded in the preceding 48 hours, and 1,643 have been killed since the October 2025 ceasefire began.

breaking.headline: NATO scraps its 2027 leaders' summit in Albania as meetings are scaled back
breaking.fact: NATO will not hold a leaders' summit in Albania in 2027 as planned, scaling back high-level meetings amid tensions over defense spending, Iran and the war in Ukraine. Defense ministers did not meet last month and none is planned for October 2027, and foreign ministers will meet once next year instead of twice. Albania's Prime Minister Edi Rama said 'for sure not in 2027' and Tirana could host in 2028; Secretary-General Mark Rutte said summits happen 'when we need them.'

weekInBrief.headline: Wholesale inflation hits 6.5%, fastest since 2022
weekInBrief.body: The Bureau of Labor Statistics reported Friday that October producer prices rose 0.3% on the month — a touch below the 0.4% expected — but 6.5% over 12 months, the largest annual rise since November 2022. Core producer prices, excluding food and energy, rose 5.0% on the year, while consumer prices run at 4%; the Federal Reserve meets Dec. 8-9, with officials leaning toward another hike.

weekInBrief.headline: Microsoft 365 outage resolved after hours-long global disruption
weekInBrief.body: Microsoft says a global outage of its Microsoft 365 services, which disrupted email and other apps for hours, has been fully resolved. The outage, which hit businesses and consumers worldwide, underscored how much daily work now depends on a single cloud provider.

weekInBrief.headline: Border crossings fall to lowest level in decades
weekInBrief.body: Illegal crossings at the U.S.-Mexico border have dropped to the lowest point in decades since President Trump resumed office, according to the New York Times. The White House is not satisfied, pressing for still lower numbers and more deportations even as the flow has collapsed.

weekInBrief.headline: Fuel crisis and protests squeeze Chile's president
weekInBrief.body: Chile's president is on the back foot after just eight months in office, squeezed by a fuel crisis and street protests, with approval at 24%, NPR reports. The ultraconservative leader's early stumble is a reminder that energy shortages bite fast, even for a government elected on a tough-on-crime, pro-market platform.

items.headline: Latest from the Strait
items.body: Washington widened the pressure campaign this weekend, standing up Task Force Iron Gate to extend the blockade from sea to land — CENTCOM said Nov. 11 that U.S. forces are now working to deny the Revolutionary Guard use of overland routes and the Caspian Sea for weapons and sanctioned goods. The blockade's toll keeps climbing: CENTCOM now puts denied Iranian crude exports at more than $30 billion, with nearly 150 vessels diverted and five disabled since July. Iran answered with a second claimed drone attack on Bahrain on Sunday, again unverified, as shipping through the strait stays about 65% below pre-conflict levels. On oil, the blockade still holds: Kpler recorded zero Iranian crude exports in September — the first such month since it began tracking in 2013 — while non-Iranian crude kept moving through the strait at about 8.5 million barrels a day in the latest Kpler week, roughly 60% of the pre-war rate, and Vortexa separately put September non-Iranian Gulf flows at 81% of pre-war levels.

space.headline: NASA hails Starship's first orbital catch; Florida launches eyed within months
space.body: NASA welcomed Saturday's milestone — Administrator Jared Isaacman praised the first tower catch of a Starship returning from orbit — and SpaceX expects to begin launching Starships from Florida's Kennedy Space Center within the next few months. Ship 42 was caught at Starbase on Saturday at 3:20 p.m. CT after 14 orbits, 22.5 hours and 26 Starlink V3 deployments. The Super Heavy booster was lost after its boostback burn ended early on a low-fuel warning — 32 of 33 engines relit — with the root cause still under investigation.

space.headline: Webb finds ice older than the star it orbits
space.body: The James Webb Space Telescope found water and carbon dioxide ice in the debris disk of Beta Pictoris, a 20-million-year-old star 64 light-years away. The water ice is glassy, not crystalline — less than 7% crystalline — and mixed with carbon dioxide in comet-like proportions, suggesting it formed in the interstellar medium before the star itself existed. The study, in Science, was led by Sarah Betti of the Space Telescope Science Institute.

space.headline: The brain's fear center doubles as a save button for memories
space.body: Cedars-Sinai researchers found amygdala neurons act like a save button for memories: in 112 epilepsy patients with implanted electrodes, neurons tuned to categories such as faces and animals fired more strongly for images the patients later remembered. The study, published Oct. 27 in Nature Neuroscience, suggests the walnut-sized structure filters which everyday experiences become lasting memories — a possible lead on memory disorders including Alzheimer's.

space.headline: Giant prehistoric rodent fossils found in Thailand
space.body: Paleontologists found fossils of Yakamys sirindhornae, a rodent that lived about 34 million years ago in southern Thailand and weighed roughly 30 kg (66 lbs) — about twice the size of other known rodents of its era. The teeth, found in a Krabi lignite mine, push the history of rodent gigantism much earlier and wider than thought; the find is published in Scientific Reports.

apod.title: Apollo 12 and Surveyor 3
apod.credit: Apollo 12, Alan Bean — Stereo Image Copyright: Kevin Frank — NASA Astronomy Picture of the Day, November 14, 2026
apod.explanation: Put on your red/blue glasses: this 3D anaglyph shows Apollo 12 astronaut Pete Conrad visiting the Surveyor 3 spacecraft on the Moon's Ocean of Storms in November 1969 — 57 years ago this week. Surveyor 3 had landed there in April 1967, and the Lunar Module Intrepid touched down less than 200 meters away; the stereo view was built from two photos taken on the lunar surface.
